header.name: Digital Hardware Design (DHD)
header.description: Field programmable gate arrays (FPGAs) are the first choice for implementation of digital systems due to their distributed and parallel architecture. FPGAs also allows complete control over arithmetic

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Students are able to design and implement sequential and combinational logic design on FPGA

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Students are able to write Verilog code to integrate on-board FPGA switches, VGA interface, memory, embedded hardware units etc.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Students are able to implement the algorithms using HLS.

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Students are able to design new IP with appropriate AXI interface

lecture_topics: Lab: Combinational logic design, Synchronous and asynchronous logic design and arithmetic circuits
weekly_plan.tutorial_assignment: Lab + Homework: Verilog code, simulation and implementation: Comparators, Decoders/Encoders, code converters, ALU, counters, pulse-width modulation, Fibonacci
Lab + Homework: Door lock code, traffic lights, sequence detectors etc.
Lab + Homework: VGA stripes, screen saver, Video game

resources.title: D. Harris and S. Harris, “Digital Design and Computer Architecture”, Morgan Kauffmann, 2012.
R. Haskell and D. Hanna, “Learning by example using Verilog advanced digital design”, LBE Books, 2014
Uwe Meyer-Baese, Digital Signal Processing with Field Programmable Gate Arrays, Springer, 2007
